1:1: This passage is read on December 24, the Eve of the Nativity of the Lord.
2:2: This passage is read on November 8, the Synaxis of Michael and All Angels.
2:11: This passage is read on March 25, the Feast of the Annunciation to the Theotokos, and on December 26, the Synaxis of the Theotokos.
4:14: This passage is read on the third Sunday of Great Lent, called the Sunday of the Adoration of the Cross.
5:4: This passage is read on days commemorating hieromartyrs.
6:13: This passage is read on days commemorating prophets.
7:7: This passage is read on February 2, the Feast of the Presentation of the Lord in the Temple.
7:26: This passage is read on days commemorating a hierarch.
9:1: A description of the Mosaic tabernacle, which prefigures the heavenly altar. This passage is read during feasts of the Virgin Mary and Advent to describe the mystery of the Incarnation of the Son of God. Mary's womb was prepared to be Christ's tabernacle, the very dwelling place of God. This passage is read on November 21, the Feast of the Entrance of the Theotokos into the Temple.
11:9: Heb 11:9, 10, 17–23, 32–40: This passage is read on the Sunday before Christmas, called the Sunday of the Holy Fathers.
11:24: This passage is read on the first Sunday of Great Lent, called the Sunday of Orthodoxy.
11:33: This passage is read on December 17, the Feast of the Prophet Daniel; on August 1, the Procession of the Cross; and on the first Sunday after Pentecost, called the Sunday of All Saints.
12:28: This passage is read on the Saturday before Palm Sunday, called Lazarus Saturday.
13:7: This passage is read on days commemorating hieromartyrs.
13:17: This passage is read on days commemorating hierarchs.
5:10: This passage is read on days commemorating prophets.
5:6: This passage is read on April 25, the Feast of St. Mark the Evangelist.
